about: Risk tiers by path (#1259 step 2), read by scripts/tier.mjs (pnpm tier). The auto rules list the harmless extensions they cover, so a file of any other kind falls to light. A file takes the highest tier of the rules whose paths match it (and whose except does not), light when none does; a test (x.test.ts, x.test-helpers.ts, a folder's tests.rs) also takes the tier of the file it tests (x.ts, the folder's mod.rs), so the guard of a deep file is deep. A change takes the highest tier of its files. Without these rules, or when they cannot be read, a change is deep. person is never given by path: it is the label tier:person, set by hand. Globs are matched against the whole path from the repository root: ** any number of folders, * and ? within one name, {a,b} either; a rule with ignoreCase matches whatever the case.

rules.why: documents and their images, which nothing runs: only these extensions (.md .txt .png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .avif .svg), so anything else under docs (a script, a template, a notebook, a Makefile) is light; AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md are left light, since every agent session follows them

data only tests read, in these formats only (.json .jsonl .txt .sql .csv .md .yaml .yml): code in a fixtures folder, a binary or anything else there is light, and so are the tests themselves (a weakened test lets a later bug through)

icons, images and fonts (and their licence notes), loaded as images and font files, never run: only these extensions (.svg .png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .avif .ico .woff .woff2 .ttf .otf .md .txt); CSS, code or anything else under it is light, since one CSS rule can hide a consent or permission card
the store and its migrations: a step runs once on every person's data, and must not break the build still serving during a swap
the trust boundaries as written: later trust decisions are checked against this text
which tools a session has, when the person is asked, project trust, app secrets and capabilities, and path containment (docs/security-boundaries.md)
who may talk to the host (tokens, proofs, origins) and what an app view may load
the desktop commands the webview may call, and its CSP
starting, keeping, swapping, updating and stopping hosts and agents, here and on linked machines (keeper, shell, centralu serve, links): bugs show only in the real environment
signed content, releases and updates: what reaches every person's machine, and how it is checked there
messages between UI, host and linked machines of different versions: additions only, and a mistake reaches every pair

the type-aware lint's lists of findings that predate it (#1339): every conversion edits them, and what keeps them shrinking is deep (tooling/lint-allowlist.ts, tooling/type-aware-lint.test.ts, which compares them with main's). When the last list goes, this rule and the except in guards go with it: tooling/tier.test.ts fails on a glob that matches nothing
the repository-wide guards and the test, lint and type setup every change is checked by: a weakened guard lets every later change through
what CI runs the UI scenarios with: Playwright's configs (retries, what runs), the flaky reporter that sets flaky=true, the web server, the UX baseline; the scenarios themselves are light
new dependencies and install scripts run on every machine that installs, CI's included
what CI runs and may skip, and the checks, merge queue and release tools that decide what lands and is published: a loosened gate lets every later change through
these rules and the code that reads them decide how much review every later change gets
